readme.text:
# Superpowers

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## Table of Contents

- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Commercial Services](#commercial-services)
- [Getting Started](#installation)
  - [Claude Code](#claude-code)
  - [Antigravity](#antigravity)
  - [Codex App](#codex-app)
  - [Codex CLI](#codex-cli)
  - [Cursor](#cursor)
  - [Devin CLI](#devin-cli)
  - [Factory Droid](#factory-droid)
  - [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli)
  - [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli)
  - [Grok Build CLI](#grok-build-cli)
  - [Kimi Code](#kimi-code)
  - [OpenCode](#opencode)
  - [Pi](#pi)
  - [Qwen Code](#qwen-code)
  - [Hermes Agent](#hermes-agent)
  - [Muse](#muse)
- [The Basic Workflow](#the-basic-workflow)
- [When Something Goes Wrong](#when-something-goes-wrong)
- [Community](#community)
- [What's Inside](#whats-inside)
- [Philosophy](#philosophy)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Updating](#updating)
- [License](#license)
- [Visual companion telemetry](#visual-companion-telemetry)

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

## Commercial Services

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

## Installation

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

### Claude Code

Superpowers is available via the [official Claude plugin marketplace](https://claude.com/plugins/superpowers)

#### Official Marketplace

- Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
  ```

#### Superpowers Marketplace

The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin from this marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Antigravity

Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

```bash
agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
```

Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the `using-superpowers` skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

### Codex App

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.
- You should see `Superpowers` in the Coding section.
- Click the `+` next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

### Codex CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- Open the plugin search interface:

  ```bash
  /plugins
  ```

- Search for Superpowers:

  ```bash
  superpowers
  ```

- Select `Install Plugin`.

### Cursor

- In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

  ```text
  /add-plugin superpowers
  ```

- Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

### Devin CLI

- Install the plugin from this repository:

  ```bash
  devin plugins install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update to the latest version with:

  ```bash
  devin plugins update superpowers
  ```

### Factory Droid

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers
  ```

### Gemini CLI

- Install the extension:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions update superpowers
  ```

### GitHub Copilot CLI

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Grok Build CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Grok plugin marketplace](https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace).

- Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust
  ```

- Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

  ```text
  /marketplace
  ```

### Kimi Code

Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

- Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

  ```text
  /plugins
  ```

- Go to `Marketplace` > `Superpowers` and install it.

- Or install directly from this repository:

  ```text
  /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.kimi.md](docs/README.kimi.md)

### OpenCode

OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

- Tell OpenCode:

  ```
  Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.opencode.md](docs/README.opencode.md)

### Pi

Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

```bash
pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers
```

For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

```bash
pi -e /path/to/superpowers
```

The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility `Skill` tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

### Qwen Code

Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

- Install the plugin from this repository, and pick `superpowers` when prompted:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions update superpowers
  ```

### Hermes Agent

Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

```bash
hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable
```

Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

### Muse

Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The `using-superpowers` bootstrap is injected via the native `SessionStart` hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

- Install from a local checkout:

  ```bash
  muse plugins install ./
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

  Or clone and install:

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
  muse plugins install ./superpowers
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  muse plugins update superpowers
  ```

Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the `SessionStart` hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send `Let's make a react todo list` — a working install auto-triggers `brainstorming` before any code is written. Version is tracked in `.version-bump.json` so `scripts/bump-version.sh` keeps it in sync.

## The Basic Workflow

1. **brainstorming** - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

2. **using-git-worktrees** - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

3. **writing-plans** - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

4. **subagent-driven-development** or **executing-plans** - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

5. **test-driven-development** - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

6. **requesting-code-review** - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

7. **finishing-a-development-branch** - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

**The agent checks for relevant skills before any task.** Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

## When Something Goes Wrong

Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the **diagnosing-superpowers** skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session `<id>`".

The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

## Community

Superpowers is built by [Jesse Vincent](https://blog.fsck.com) and the rest of the folks at [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com).

- **Discord**: [Join us](https://discord.gg/35wsABTejz) for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers
- **Issues**: https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues
- **Release announcements**: [Sign up](https://primeradiant.com/superpowers/) to get notified about new versions

## What's Inside

### Skills Library

**Testing**
- **test-driven-development** - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

**Debugging**
- **systematic-debugging** - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)
- **verification-before-completion** - Ensure it's actually fixed
- **diagnosing-superpowers** - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

**Collaboration** 
- **brainstorming** - Drawing out intent before building
- **writing-plans** - Detailed implementation plans
- **executing-plans** - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review
- **dispatching-parallel-agents** - Concurrent subagent workflows
- **requesting-code-review** - Pre-review checklist
- **receiving-code-review** - Responding to feedback
- **using-git-worktrees** - Parallel development branches
- **finishing-a-development-branch** - Merge/PR decision workflow
- **subagent-driven-development** - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)

**Meta**
- **writing-skills** - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)
- **using-superpowers** - Introduction to the skills system

## Philosophy

- **Test-Driven Development** - Write tests first, always
- **Systematic over ad-hoc** - Process over guessing
- **Complexity reduction** - Simplicity as primary goal
- **Evidence over claims** - Verify before declaring success

Read [the original release announcement](https://blog.fsck.com/2025/10/09/superpowers/).

## Contributing

The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support.

1. Fork the repository
2. Switch to the 'dev' branch
3. Create a branch for your work
4. Follow the `writing-skills` skill for creating and testing new and modified skills
5. Submit a PR, being sure to fill in the pull request template.

Skill-behavior tests use the drill eval harness from [superpowers-evals](https://github.com/prime-radiant-inc/superpowers-evals/), cloned into `evals/` — see `evals/README.md` for setup. Plugin-infrastructure tests live at `tests/` and run via the relevant `run-*.sh` or `npm test`.

See `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md` for the complete guide.

## Updating

Superpowers updates are somewhat coding-agent dependent, but are often automatic.

## License

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details

## Visual companion telemetry

Because skills and plugins don't provide any feedback to creators, we have no idea how many of you are using Superpowers. By default, the Prime Radiant logo on brainstorming's optional visual companion feature is loaded from our website. It includes the version of Superpowers in use. It does not include any details about your project, prompt, or coding agent. We don't see your clicks or anything about what you're building. This helps us have a rough idea of how many folks are using Superpowers and which version of Superpowers they're using. It's 100% optional. To disable this, set the environment variable `SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` to any true value. Superpowers also honors Claude Code's `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` opt-outs.

relevance.instructions: Using only state.repository and state.rules, does this repository document an AI agent tool, workflow, skill, agent-specific infrastructure, a curated collection of agent resources, or its own agent integration? An owned MCP package is an agent integration even when the main product is general-purpose.

criteria.true: Yes. At least one of the listed agent-related deliverables, integrations, or curated resources is documented.
criteria.false: No. None is documented. Theoretical use of generic software by an agent and incidental mentions alone do not qualify.

label.form.tools.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes runnable agent-related programs actually shipped by this repository? Policy illustrations only, not repository evidence: (1) This repository documents runnable shell/Node test programs for its own agent plugin infrastructure: supported, even when the plugin mainly delivers skills and the test programs are not standalone products. (2) An agent task skill tells its host to run tests on a user project, but no runnable helper belonging to this repository is documented: not_supported from those host commands alone.

criteria.supported: The supplied text documents at least one executable agent-related program implemented or distributed by this repository: a CLI, application, client, server, service/API or executable utility. Optional programs and executables that test agent components qualify. It documents an actual repository deliverable, not merely a command for an external host or a program generated as a task output. A documented executable helper bundled with an owned agent skill or plugin qualifies; it need not be a standalone application.
criteria.not_supported: No runnable agent-related program is documented as belonging to this repository. Libraries alone, general utilities without documented agent functionality or an owned agent integration, and external programs linked from a catalog do not qualify. Skill instructions, prompts or templates executed through an external agent host alone do not establish a program shipped by this repository. Calling task skills tools does not establish a runnable program.

label.form.skills.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's skills?

criteria.supported: This repository documents its own reusable agent task skills or instruction packages. A local SKILL.md package, a skill bundled with a plugin/product, or explicitly built-in/preloaded skills provisioned by the product qualify; built-in skills need not show their file paths.
criteria.not_supported: No owned agent task skill is documented. Links to skills in other repositories, general explanations of the skill format, and blank skill-authoring templates do not establish an owned skill.

label.form.extensions.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's plugins and configuration?

criteria.supported: This repository documents an installable agent plugin or non-skill agent configuration: MCP client launch settings, hooks, slash commands, subagent definitions, harness rules/configuration or interface extensions. Built-in agent profiles and agent-specific launch, prompt or model settings also qualify. A plugin installation/invocation command pointing to this repository or a local plugin directory (for example, claude --plugin-dir ./...) establishes an owned plugin, including one that bundles skills. MCP client configuration supplied inline in this README is a configuration deliverable, even when the configured server belongs to another repository.
criteria.not_supported: No plugin or non-skill agent configuration is documented. SKILL.md packages, their top-level skill router, and copying skill folders into a skills directory are skill delivery alone. External plugin links or general plugin usage instructions do not establish an owned plugin. Generic product/server/trainer settings alone are not agent configuration. General document-conversion or OCR plugins without agent-plugin or harness-configuration functionality do not qualify.

label.form.workflows.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's workflows and frameworks?

criteria.supported: This repository provides an agent task workflow, an agent orchestration framework, or an SDK for building agents. Documentation of any one is sufficient.
criteria.not_supported: The supplied text documents none of these agent workflows, frameworks or SDKs. Ordinary CI alone does not qualify.

label.form.catalogs.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's catalogs and reference?

criteria.supported: This repository is primarily a curated collection of agent resources, reference materials or guides. Its curated entries may be external.
criteria.not_supported: The supplied text does not establish primary curation of agent resources, references or guides. Merely documenting the use of an owned product does not make it primarily a catalog.

label.purpose.development.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's development and operations?

criteria.supported: This repository's deliverables or actual curated content support software development, testing, deployment, infrastructure operations, system security or designing, building or integrating AI agent applications or their components. Any one documented use is enough. Documented guidance and authoring workflows for these activities qualify; producing final application code is not required.
criteria.not_supported: No such intended use is documented for the deliverables or actual curated content. Being implemented in code or ordinary repository maintenance alone does not qualify.

label.purpose.office.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes the documented user tasks of this repository's deliverables or actual curated content?

criteria.supported: This repository's deliverables or actual curated content support document handling (creating, editing, parsing or converting documents), personal productivity, job search or career planning, accessibility, customer support, communication or project/team coordination. Documented communication relays and personal-productivity use cases qualify even when the main product is developer infrastructure. Any one documented use is enough; document creation and editing qualify.
criteria.not_supported: The supplied text documents none of these uses for the deliverables or actual curated content.

label.purpose.content.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes the user content, writing or design tasks supported by this repository?

criteria.supported: The repository's actual deliverables or actual curated content support at least one user purpose: writing, visual design, creative media, business content, or marketing. Visual design includes application UI or graphics. One documented matching feature or creator workflow qualifies even when the main product is developer-facing; a dedicated content product is not required.
criteria.not_supported: No such user content or marketing purpose is documented. PRDs, technical specifications and implementation plans generated within a coding workflow alone do not qualify. This repository's own documentation, illustrations or promotional material alone do not establish a user content purpose.

label.purpose.research.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes the analysis, research, investigation or information/data visualization uses of this repository?

criteria.supported: The actual product, supplied skills or actual curated content explicitly support at least one user task: analysis, research, investigation, or information/data visualization. These are alternatives; visualization does not require a research task. Support may be direct or prepare inputs for the task. Text/data analysis, technical/scientific research, debugging and root-cause/security investigation qualify. A built-in research or investigation agent/skill used during development qualifies.
criteria.not_supported: No such use is attributed to the actual product, supplied skills or curated entries. Introductory examples of what agents or skill formats can do in general, this product's own research paper or benchmark results, and document/spreadsheet handling without a stated analysis, research, investigation or information/data visualization use do not establish this purpose. Artistic design or visual styling alone is not information/data visualization.

label.purpose.learning.instructions: Using only state.repository and applying state.rules, does any actual deliverable or actual curated entry support knowledge organization or human learning, teaching or study? Ordinary installation and usage instructions alone do not establish this purpose; explicitly educational materials still count when teaching this product. Evaluate delivered functionality and actual resource descriptions. Any one matching use is sufficient, including optional components and external curated entries.

criteria.true: At least one actual deliverable or actual curated entry has either purpose: (1) organize or manage reusable user/project knowledge, including user-note management and organizing facts, documents or knowledge bases for reuse; teaching is not required; (2) help people learn, teach or study. Purpose (2) includes courses, study/coaching resources, tools for teaching operations such as classes/rosters/coursework management, skill implementations or reference materials explicitly offered as educational material for people, including examples and design-pattern references, and user documentation/diagram or knowledge-sharing workflows explicitly intended to support organizational learning. These are alternatives: one matching use is sufficient. Actual optional components and curated external resources qualify; a dedicated education product, full curriculum, interface, separate educational component or implementation of external catalog entries is not required.
criteria.false: Neither knowledge organization nor helping people learn/teach/study is documented for any actual deliverable or actual curated entry. Instructions, methodology or workflow guidance addressed to an agent for coding or other business tasks alone are not educational material for people. Ordinary instructions for installing/using this product and an index of its own documentation alone do not establish either purpose. Ordinary internal data structures alone are not a knowledge-organization use. Generic communication or document rendering without a documented knowledge/learning purpose alone is insufficient. A generic heading or table-of-contents anchor with no description of a matching knowledge-management or people-education use does not establish either purpose.

label.capability.orchestration.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's orchestration and automation?

criteria.supported: This repository documents how an owned mechanism advances task stages, continues execution, coordinates agents, or performs actions in another application. A described multi-step task skill or pipeline qualifies; an owned execution engine is not required. Any one documented mechanism is enough, including an optional component.
criteria.not_supported: No such concrete task-progression, continuation, coordination or application-action mechanism is documented. General claims that skills complete, repeat or automate tasks, task-output names, and plugin installation/activation steps are insufficient. External orchestration or automation projects merely listed here do not qualify.

label.capability.memory.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes the agent memory or knowledge retrieval provided by this repository? Policy illustrations only, not repository evidence: (1) A supplied reusable skill searches and reads pages from a knowledge base or wiki for an agent, through a third-party API: supported. (2) A supplied retrieval-and-reasoning agent example: supported. (3) A career-advice skill searches job openings and imports a resume only within that career task: not_supported. (4) A catalog links to an external memory or document-retrieval project but supplies no own retrieval component: not_supported.

criteria.supported: This repository documents an agent memory/context-management mechanism, an owned retrieval-agent example, or a reusable agent component with operations that search or read material from knowledge sources such as documents, wikis, databases, documentation sites or scientific literature. A knowledge-source connector qualifies through those retrieval operations even if it also edits or organizes the source; retrieval need not be the component's sole or main function. An owned retrieval-agent example need not be the main product or a reusable API. A RAG index is not required. A documented owned agent memory/context component qualifies even when optional, experimental, default-off, or backed by an external memory service.
criteria.not_supported: None of those agent memory/context mechanisms, knowledge-source retrieval components or owned retrieval-agent examples is documented. Search or import within another business task, such as job search or resume import, is insufficient. Task documents, interview stories, skill-context advice and external project links alone do not qualify.

label.capability.evaluation.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes evaluation or observation of agents provided by this repository? Policy illustrations only, not repository evidence: (1) A coding workflow checks its generated diff against requirements and runs lint, type checks and unit tests: not_supported, because it checks task artifacts. (2) A project journal preserves completed work and context for the next coding session: not_supported. (3) A supplied tool retrieves an agent run tree with model/tool calls, errors and latency from an external tracing service: supported. (4) A benchmark runs or compares agents on tasks to assess their behavior: supported. (5) A bundled diagnostic task skill reads local agent session transcripts and reports execution evidence: supported; reading existing host traces is observation, without an owned recorder or tracing server.

criteria.supported: This repository provides a mechanism whose measured or observed subject is an AI agent's behavior or execution. Testing or comparing agent behavior, recording/displaying/retrieving execution events or session traces, displaying an agent's running/completed status or issuing notifications based on that status, and tracking agent usage or cost qualify. A bundled tool or skill retrieving agent execution traces qualifies even when the tracing service is external. Manual steps and optional components may qualify; an automatic agent launcher or an owned tracing backend is not required. A supplied terminal or chat renderer that displays agent tool-call events and their execution statuses qualifies; it need not operate the agent. An owned diagnostic skill that reads agent session transcripts and reports what the agent executed or where its behavior failed also qualifies; the transcripts may be stored by the external agent host.
criteria.not_supported: No such agent-behavior evaluation or execution-observation mechanism is documented. Checking code, websites, accessibility or other task artifacts is not evaluation of the agent itself. Ordinary repository CI, project journals kept as context for later tasks, and environment switching alone do not establish agent evaluation or observation. Product benchmark numbers and external project links alone are insufficient.

label.capability.runtime.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes this repository's model and runtime management?

criteria.supported: This repository provides mechanisms to install, adapt or distribute agent/harness components, or manage model routing, provider access, permissions, isolation or runtime configuration. Owned installers, generation of harness-specific agent/skill/command configurations with permission mappings, adapters and model proxies/gateways qualify. An owned agent or task-skill runner with model-provider access or inference settings also qualifies. Model or effort selection and reasoning/token budgets exposed by an owned agent service/API are runtime controls.
criteria.not_supported: No owned agent model/runtime management mechanism is documented. Manually copying skills or using an external host plugin/marketplace command to install this repository skills alone does not establish an owned installer, adapter or runtime manager. Recommending models or linking external runtime components alone does not qualify.

label.capability.interaction.instructions: Using only state.repository as evidence and applying state.rules, which statement describes the agent interaction or external application integrations provided by this repository? Policy illustrations only, not repository evidence: (1) A local document task skill is installed and invoked through its agent host or the host API: not_supported from that host usage alone. (2) An owned task skill imports profile data from an external application through a third-party gateway: supported, even without an owned backend. (3) A workflow installer generates task/rule configurations for compatible agent hosts but provides no additional interface feature or application connection: not_supported. (4) An owned renderer improves the agent interface, or an owned component provides voice/remote control/notifications: supported.

criteria.supported: This repository provides agent voice, remote control, notifications, interface enhancements, or an owned component that connects agents to an external application/API. Documented reading, fetching or importing data from an external application qualifies as an integration, as do modifying data or performing other actions there. An owned plugin or task skill qualifies even when it uses an external gateway/service; it need not own the external backend. Owned optional service adapters or executable API-processing examples also qualify. The interaction or connection must be functionality described for the owned component, beyond that component merely being installed, loaded or invoked by an agent host.
criteria.not_supported: No owned agent interaction or explicit application/API integration is documented. Merely listing external integrations or giving generic task instructions without an explicit integration does not qualify. Installing, loading or invoking task skills through a host, including its API, and generating compatible host task/rule configurations alone do not establish an interface enhancement or external application connection.
